scope: Synthetic timing and provenance labels only; no external or market-derived observations are included.
fail_closed_rule: A candidate input may be considered only when its documented identity, bar label/timezone, and recorded availability at or before the N225 decision are all established. A missing or ambiguous premise is not repaired by inference or by another source.

cases.setup: A candidate record has a documented source-created time, bar-start label, timezone, and a separately documented availability time that is no later than the abstract N225 decision time.
cases.reason: Even a known ordering needs a frozen policy defining which documented availability field governs and how it is retained for later reproduction.

cases.setup: A later provider correction would replace information previously associated with an earlier candidate record, while the former vintage and its availability history are absent.
cases.reason: A later correction cannot stand in for the information demonstrably available at the earlier decision time.

cases.setup: The candidate record lacks either a documented timezone or an unambiguous statement that its label is a bar start, bar end, or observation creation time.
cases.reason: Its ordering relative to the N225 decision cannot be established from an ambiguous label.

cases.setup: The abstract N225 decision occurs before the candidate record's documented availability time, irrespective of any earlier source-created or bar-label time.
cases.reason: The input was not available at the decision and therefore cannot enter that decision.

cases.setup: The candidate distribution has a documented session break, holiday, halt, or absent interval and the source supplies no rule assigning a usable meaning to the gap.
cases.reason: No continuity, carry-forward, or synthetic replacement is permitted without a documented source rule.

cases.setup: Two providers would describe non-identical candidate records or timing metadata for the same abstract interval.
cases.reason: This task admits one provider only; a discrepancy cannot be resolved by combining providers or choosing retrospectively.
